sections.title: People-group terminology
sections.intro: These are the most definitionally precise terms on the site. The Definitions page gives exact numeric thresholds; translations must carry those thresholds intact.

fields: "An ethnolinguistic group who perceive themselves to have a common affinity for one another based on language, culture, religion, and worldview … the largest possible group within which the gospel can spread as a viable, indigenous church-planting movement without encountering barriers of understanding or acceptance." (Definitions page)

This is the fundamental unit of measurement for the entire site. The concept is ethnic/linguistic, not political — "people group" must not be rendered as "nation-state", "tribe" (with primitive connotations), or "social group". An imprecise translation invalidates every statistic.
"Has approximately 2 disciples or fewer out of 100 (≤ 2%) and lacks the capacity to establish indigenous churches without cross-cultural assistance." (Definitions page)

The threshold (≤ 2%) must be reproducible in the translation. The concept of lack of capacity for self-propagation is as important as the percentage. Avoid wording that implies the group is spiritually "unchosen" or socially marginal.

A people group with no known believers or a tiny few and lacking the four primary levels of effective engagement (apostolic effort in residence; commitment to the local culture and heart language; long-term ministry commitment; sowing the gospel aimed at a CPM). (Definitions page)
"2,085 unengaged people groups" / "Unengaged people groups have no missionaries, no churches, and often no known believers." (Adopt page)

"Unengaged" is a technical term meaning no active church-planting work, not "socially unengaged" or "emotionally unresponsive". A mistranslation here obscures the entire urgency of the site's call to action.
The combined category — unreached AND lacking the four levels of effective engagement. The research page uses "Find a UUPG" as a UI label.
"Daily prayer for each of the 2,085 UUPGs" (Vision page)
UUPG is an established acronym in global missions. Keep a stable equivalent acronym (e.g., "UUPG") or a consistently used phrase in each language to align with international prayer tools.
"Has approximately 1 disciple or fewer out of 100 (≤ 1%). More church planting teams are needed to increase fruitful engagement." (Definitions page)
"Fruitful engagement among frontier peoples and the under-engaged" (homepage)
The hyphenated compound form appears consistently. Convey that work has begun but is insufficient in scale — not that the people themselves are indifferent.

"Has approximately 1 disciple or fewer out of 1,000 (≤ 0.1%) with no confirmed, sustained movement to Jesus. Often geographically isolated with little to no access to the gospel; pioneer work generally must begin with nonbelievers." (Definitions page)

"Frontier" signals the missiological cutting-edge — the most unreached of the unreached. Avoid military connotations where culturally sensitive; preserve the sense of work among them might be their "first-ever" gospel contact.
The technical descriptor of what constitutes a people group (shared language, culture, religion, worldview). Not used as a standalone label in the UI, but embedded in the Definitions page definition.
Translators should understand this is the underlying concept so they choose ethnicity/language-oriented words, not political ones.

"There is sustained activity to share Christ and make disciples; there are efforts to establish self-sustaining churches; the work occurs in culturally appropriate and locally relevant ways." For WAGF: cross-cultural workers are resident.
"To engage every Unengaged People Group by 2033" (Priority)

"Engagement" is a precision term — resident, sustained, cross-cultural, CPM-oriented. A vague rendering like "involvement" or "contact" strips the core meaning. The whole priority statement depends on it.
Engagement that is visibly producing disciples and churches, not just activity. Used in homepage goals and the About page declaration.
"Fruitful, long-term, residential engagement of the world's unengaged peoples" (Sending Summit Declaration)
The qualifier "fruitful" is theologically and strategically intentional — it distinguishes activity from results.
The condition of a people group having the gospel available to them — through workers, churches, or gospel content. Its absence is the defining tragedy of unengaged people groups.
"They have no gospel access" (Adopt page heading); "A church-led commitment to pray, give, and send so that gospel access begins" (Adopt page)
"Access" implies availability and reachability, not just geographic presence. Mistranslating as "gospel knowledge" or "gospel hearing" changes the meaning subtly but importantly.
Active, ongoing proclamation and living-out of the gospel among a people group; used in the prayer context ("prepare the way for gospel engagement through prayer").
"Help prepare the way for gospel engagement through prayer" (Pray page)
Distinct from "gospel access" (availability) — "gospel engagement" is the active missional work itself. Avoid rendering as a marketing or media campaign.
"A multiplication of indigenous churches planting churches that includes at least four streams of four spiritual generations together totaling more than 1,000 persons." (Definitions page)
"Church planting movements among every unreached people on earth" (homepage goal)

"Movement" implies self-multiplying momentum, not a single church plant or program. The metrics (4 streams × 4 generations × 1,000 persons) must be translatable; avoid wording that sounds like a social or political movement.
A church arising from within the people group that is self-sustaining and maturing in the "five selfs".
"There is an indigenous church planted among every people group on earth" (Vision goals); "lacks the capacity to establish indigenous churches without cross-cultural assistance" (Definitions)
"Indigenous" means locally rooted and self-governing, not "native religion" or "animist". Clarify if necessary to avoid syncretism associations.
The five markers of a mature indigenous church: self-propagating, self-governing, self-supporting, self-theologizing, self-missionizing. (Definitions page)
This is a standard missions framework. Translators should use established equivalents if they exist in the target language; if not, each "self-" compound needs a consistent rendering.
Cross-cultural workers who live among the people group (not remote or visiting). A requirement for WAGF's definition of engagement.
"Cross-cultural workers are resident" (Vision page); "Apostolic (pioneering) effort in residence" (Definitions page)
"Resident" versus "nonresident" is a key distinction on the site. Translations must not flatten this to simply "missionaries".
Mission workers from a different culture serving among a people group. Used as the preferred term over "missionary" in some contexts.
"lacks the capacity to establish indigenous churches without cross-cultural assistance" (Definitions)
The "cross-cultural" qualifier is intentional — these are not workers from within the group. Use a term that conveys cultural difference, not just "foreign".
Front-edge mission work that begins where there are no churches or believers. One of the four criteria for a people group being "engaged".
"Apostolic" here means sent/pioneering, not a denominational title. The parenthetical "(pioneering)" signals this; retain that clarity in translation.
The initial evangelism phase among a frontier people group where there are no believers to begin with.
"Pioneer work generally must begin with nonbelievers" (Definitions page)
Translators should convey "starting from scratch" in terms of gospel presence.
A person's first/mother tongue — the language in which they think and feel most deeply.
"Commitment to work in the local culture and heart language" (Definitions page)
A well-established missions phrase. Distinguish from "official language" or "trade language". The concept is that gospel and discipleship work must happen in this language to be fully effective.
A collective, multiplying movement of people from a group turning to follow Jesus — as opposed to isolated conversions.
"No confirmed, sustained movement to Jesus" (frontier people group definition)
This is specifically about a sustained, multiplying spiritual movement, not individual conversion or social activism.

Churches, agencies, or individuals who support engagement from outside the field — through prayer, giving, Bible translation, media, etc. Broader engagement includes important contributing components that can be done by nonresident partners.

"Broader engagement includes important contributing components that can be done by nonresident partners, including intercessory prayer, Bible translation, compassion/disaster ministry outreaches…" (Definitions page)
Helps people understand they can participate in mission even without going to the field.

The contributing (but not sufficient alone) elements of mission that nonresident partners can do: intercessory prayer, Bible translation, compassion/disaster ministry, media reach, mobilization efforts, leadership training, work among diaspora.
"Broader engagement includes important contributing components" (Definitions page)
This list clarifies that adoption and prayer are genuine participation in the mission, even without going.
Members of a people group living outside their homeland. Listed as a component of broader engagement.
Often a loanword in many languages; if so, it may be kept. Clarify it means scattered communities of a people group, not refugees in general.
Committing to pray for a specific unengaged people group every day, typically using the daily prayer guide from Doxa.Life.
"Choose an unengaged people group you will commit to pray for daily." (Pray page)
"Daily" is intentional and describes a consistent every-day commitment. Avoid rendering it as "regular prayer" or "occasional prayer".
A person who commits to pray on behalf of a UUPG. Goal: 100+ daily intercessors per UUPG.
"Raise up 100+ daily intercessors to pray for each UUPG." (Adopt page)
Use the established church term for intercessor/prayer warrior, not a courtroom or governmental connotation.
Prayer offered on behalf of others — specifically for people groups who have no one praying for them.
Distinguish from personal devotional prayer; emphasize the on behalf of others dimension.

entries.term: Daily prayer guide / daily prayer points
fields: The daily email or content resource that Doxa.Life sends to registered intercessors — including Scripture themes, prayer needs from the field, photos, stories, and key insights about the people group.

"Receive daily prayer points and join believers worldwide in prayer" (homepage); "Your daily prayer guide: Scripture-centered prayer themes, Spirit-led reflection and guidance, Real prayer needs from the field, Photos, stories and testimonies, Key insights about the people group" (Pray)
The "guide" and "points" are distinct from general devotionals — they are specific, people-group-focused, field-connected.
A theological conviction that intercession creates spiritual conditions for gospel breakthroughs before workers even arrive.
"Prayer softens hearts, opens doors, and invites the work of the Holy Spirit long before workers arrive or the gospel is proclaimed." (Pray page)
A key motivational phrase used to explain why prayer is the first step of engagement, not just a supplement to it.
A biblical title for Jesus (Matthew 9:38), used in the call to pray that He would send workers to the unengaged.
"Pray earnestly to the Lord of the harvest … that He would send laborers to the [Unengaged]." (Pray page)
Align with the established Bible translation phrase in the target language. The agricultural metaphor (harvest = people ready to respond) should carry over.
A formal, long-term church-led commitment to pray, give, and send so that gospel access begins for a specific unengaged people group.
"A church-led commitment to pray, give, and send so that gospel access begins" (Adopt page)
Avoid family-law adoption language (children, legal custody). The concept is missional sponsorship/commitment — a church takes strategic responsibility for a people group's engagement.
The three pillars of adoption — intercessory prayer, financial support, and sending workers.
"Churches and networks take ownership – praying, giving, and preparing the way for gospel workers." (homepage); "Partner through prayer, giving, and sending" (Adopt page)
This triad is used consistently. All three actions should be translated with active, participatory verbs, not passive or devotional ones.
Raising up and activating intercessors and participants across a congregation or network.
"Raise up 100+ daily intercessors" / "Tools to mobilize prayer and participation across your congregation" (Adopt page)
"Mobilize" implies active movement toward a goal. Avoid passive words like "inform" or "invite".
Organizations authorized to recruit, train, support, and send missionaries. DOXA works with but does not replace sending agencies.
"Every World Assemblies of God Fellowship affiliated missions department (129 different sending agencies as of 2026) is automatically a DOXA partner." (About page)
A technical term in mission structures. Translators should use the established local equivalent if one exists.
The framing metaphor for the mission — engaging every people group is the church's collective gift of worship to Jesus.
"Our gift to Jesus: Engage every people by 2033" (homepage)
A motivational/worshipful frame. Should feel sacrificial and offering-like, not transactional.

entries.term: Priority — "Engage every Unengaged People Group by 2033"
fields: The time-bound, measurable strategic focus of Doxa.Life.
"To engage every Unengaged People Group by 2033" (Vision page)
"Priority" signals this is the single most important strategic objective, not one among many. The 2033 deadline must be kept exact.
The overarching vision heading in the UI, referring to the 2033 goals listed on the Vision page.
A proper-noun label for the initiative's goal set. Keep the year intact.

entries.term: Every tribe, tongue, people, and nation
fields: The biblical vision from Revelation 7:9 — the picture of ultimate worship that motivates the mission.
"Jesus is worthy of glory from every tribe, tongue, people, and nation." (About page — Sending Summit Declaration)

Align with the established Bible translation in the target language. All four nouns are theologically intentional — tribe (clan/family), tongue (language), people (ethnic group), nation (political unit) — each capturing a different dimension of human diversity.

entries.term: A multitude of every people around the throne
fields: The eschatological worship scene of Revelation 7:9; the ultimate goal motivating all engagement.
"One day there will be a multitude of every people around the throne worshipping God." (About page)
Align with local Bible translation phrasing. Should feel worshipful and ultimate, not merely organizational.
Missionaries who serve within the Doxa.Life partnership network, coordinated through sending agencies.
"Partnership" signals these are not DOXA employees but workers from member agencies collaborating through the network.
